\section[la questura]{la questura — the police headquarters}

\label{lesson:IT-C447-questura}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the cloister, then the Italian for to wander.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la questura}
\textbf{la questura} — \textquotedblleft{}the police headquarters\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Per il passaporto devi andare in questura.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{For a passport you need to go to the police headquarters.}
\end{quote}

Run by \emph{il questore}; you go there for a lost passport too.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{questura} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{quaestūra} 'the office of a quaestor', from \emph{quaerere} 'to seek, to inquire' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la questura}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la questura}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la questura}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the cloister, then the Italian for to wander, then say \emph{la questura} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la questura mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The police headquarters\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la prefettura]{la prefettura — the prefecture (the local office of the state)}

\label{lesson:IT-C447-prefettura}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to wander, then the Italian for the police headquarters.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la prefettura}
\textbf{la prefettura} — \textquotedblleft{}the prefecture (the local office of the state)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La prefettura è nel palazzo in piazza.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The prefecture is in the building on the square.}
\end{quote}

The office of \emph{il prefetto}, the state's representative in a province.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{prefettura} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{praefectūra} 'the office of a prefect', from \emph{praefectus} 'one put in charge', built on \emph{facere} 'to make' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la prefettura}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la prefettura}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la prefettura}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to wander, then the Italian for the police headquarters, then say \emph{la prefettura} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la prefettura mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The prefecture (the local office of the state)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la caserma]{la caserma — the barracks; the police station (of the carabinieri)}

\label{lesson:IT-C447-caserma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the police headquarters, then the Italian for the prefecture.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la caserma}
\textbf{la caserma} — \textquotedblleft{}the barracks; the police station (of the carabinieri)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La caserma dei carabinieri è in fondo alla strada.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The carabinieri station is at the end of the street.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La caserma dei vigili del fuoco} — the fire station.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{caserma} is usually traced through French \emph{caserne} and Provençal to Latin \emph{quaterna} 'a set of four': first a small hut for four soldiers. It came into Italian as a borrowing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the police headquarters, then the Italian for the prefecture, then say \emph{la caserma} again
\end{itemize}

\section[segnalare]{segnalare — to report, to point out}

\label{lesson:IT-C447-segnalare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the prefecture, then the Italian for the barracks.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: segnalare}
\textbf{segnalare} — \textquotedblleft{}to report, to point out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho segnalato il furto alla polizia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I reported the theft to the police.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La segnalazione} — a report, a notice.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{segnalare} is built on \emph{segnale} 'signal', a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{signāle}, from \emph{signum} 'sign' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{segnalare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{segnalare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the prefecture, then the Italian for the barracks, then say \emph{segnalare} again
\end{itemize}

\section[la carta d'identità]{la carta d'identità — the identity card}

\label{lesson:IT-C447-carta-d-identita}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the barracks, then the Italian for to report.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la carta d'identità}
\textbf{la carta d'identità} — \textquotedblleft{}the identity card\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
In albergo chiedono la carta d'identità.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At the hotel they ask for your identity card.}
\end{quote}

You get it from \emph{il comune}, the town hall.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{carta d'identità} is built from \emph{carta} 'paper, card', inherited from Latin \emph{charta}, and \emph{identità}, a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{identitās}, from \emph{idem} 'the same' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la carta d'identità}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la carta d'identità}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la carta d'identità}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the barracks, then the Italian for to report, then say \emph{la carta d'identità} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
